name: McpAmount
description: Transaction amount on an MCP tool call. PingGateway sends it as both Amount and TransactionAmount (p1az-decision.groovy); default 0 keeps the bands inert for non-transactional tools instead of resolving INDETERMINATE.

name: McpDecisionContext
description: Which decision context the caller is in — McpToolCall for a tools/call. Default '' so these rules cannot fire on a request that did not declare one.

name: McpAcr
description: Authentication context class of the caller. Default 'none' — an omitted ACR is treated as NO strong authentication, so step-up fails closed.

name: McpHitlApproved
description: Set to 'true' by PingGateway only after it has verified an approved, unexpired HITL receipt bound to this user/agent/tool/amount. Default 'false' — an omitted value is never treated as consent.

name: McpUseCaseId
description: Business context the call was initiated under, forwarded by PingGateway from the BFF's X-Use-Case-Id header. Lets policy gate on INTENT rather than amount — the CIBA demo is amount-independent by design. Only ever used to REQUIRE a gate, so a missing or forged value cannot weaken a decision.

name: IsMcpToolCall
description: The request is an MCP tools/call. Every band below references this so these rules stay inert in the Transaction and tools/list contexts.

name: McpExceedsDenyLimit
description: MCP tool call whose amount is over the hard ceiling (2000). Matches the deny constant already present in this environment; the demo's $2500 case lands here.

name: McpExceedsStepUpLimit
description: MCP tool call over 500 where the caller has not completed multi-factor auth. The demo's $600 case lands here. A caller returning with Acr=Multi_Factor no longer matches, which is how a completed step-up discharges the gate.

name: McpRequiresHitlConsent
description: MCP tool call over 250 with no verified HITL receipt. The demo's $300 case lands here. A retry carrying HitlApproved=true (set by PingGateway only after verifying the receipt against the HITL service) no longer matches, which discharges the gate.

name: McpRequiresDecoupledApproval
description: MCP tool call initiated under the decoupled-approval (CIBA) use case. Deliberately has NO amount term: CIBA models "this sensitive, agent-initiated action needs out-of-band approval", not a dollar gate, which is why the demo amount is a small $150 that no amount band would catch.

name: MCP Deny — Amount Limit Exceeded
description: Hard deny: the amount is over the ceiling. Not an obligation — no retry can satisfy it.
payload: MCP tool call amount {{81f4b827-2161-447e-a810-60004f8a2058}} exceeds the maximum permitted amount.

name: MCP Permit — Step-Up Required
description: Step-up obligation. The code normalizes to STEPUP, which authorizeObligations.js and PingGateway both classify as step-up (it outranks consent when both fire).
payload: MCP tool call amount {{81f4b827-2161-447e-a810-60004f8a2058}} requires step-up authentication before it can proceed.

name: MCP Permit — HITL Consent Required
description: Consent obligation. The code normalizes to HITLCONSENT, which both readers classify as consent — PingGateway turns it into a 428 plus a HITL challenge.
payload: MCP tool call amount {{81f4b827-2161-447e-a810-60004f8a2058}} requires human approval before it can proceed.

name: MCP Permit — Amount Within Limits
description: Catch-all approval so a call matching no band still resolves to a decision.
payload: MCP tool call amount is within policy limits.

name: MCP Deny Over Limit
description: DENY when an MCP tool call exceeds the hard ceiling. DenyOverrides means this wins over the obligation rules below when several bands match at once.

name: MCP Require Step-Up
description: PERMIT with a step-up obligation when an MCP tool call is over the step-up threshold and MFA has not been completed.

name: MCP Require Decoupled Approval for the CIBA Use Case
description: PERMIT with a step-up obligation when the call runs under the decoupled-approval use case and MFA has not been completed. Amount-independent on purpose. The gateway emits the same 428 as any other step-up; the BFF resolves step_up_method=ciba from the use-case catalog on relay, so the agent drives the out-of-band flow rather than a device-list prompt.

name: MCP Require HITL Consent for Mid-Value Calls
description: PERMIT with a consent obligation when an MCP tool call is over the consent threshold and carries no verified HITL receipt. An amount over the step-up threshold matches this rule too; the readers resolve that by precedence (step-up outranks consent), so no extra condition is needed here to exclude the higher band.

name: MCP Permit Within Limits
description: PERMIT everything not caught above. Every policy needs exactly one catch-all with condition {empty:{}}, or a call matching no rule resolves INDETERMINATE — which both gateways read as "a human must approve" and would turn into a spurious 428.

name: MCP Tool Call Amount Bands
description: Amount bands for the MCP decision endpoint, so a gateway that makes only the MCP call still gets an amount-aware gate. Rules: (1) DENY over 2000; (2) PERMIT+step-up over 500 without MFA; (3) PERMIT+step-up for the decoupled-approval use case, amount-independent; (4) PERMIT+HITL-consent over 250 without a verified receipt; (5) PERMIT otherwise. Every rule is gated on DecisionContext=McpToolCall.

name: MCP Amount Bands
description: Root policy set for the MCP amount bands. DenyOverrides with evaluateAll=true: every child policy is evaluated and any DENY wins, so this composes with the existing MCP audience/actor-chain rules rather than replacing them.
